column2: Native GitHub Copilot support in SSMS starts with version {{c1::22}}.
column3:
SSMS 22 introduced the native integration. Enable it by selecting the AI Assistance workload for that installation.
Review source

column2: The Fabric tenant setting for Azure OpenAI-powered Copilot access is {{c1::Users can use Copilot and other features powered by Azure OpenAI}}.
column3:
A Fabric administrator controls this setting. Enablement for the user still does not replace eligible capacity or workspace permissions.
Review source

column2: The SSMS Copilot chat sign-in screen offers {{c1::Copilot Free}} for users without existing Copilot access.
column3:
This is an option at sign-in if you do not already have Copilot access. The GitHub account used for Copilot is separate from your database connection.
Review source

column2: If Copilot lacks database-specific context, first check for an active {{c1::database connection}}.
column3:
Confirm that the connection points to the intended database. The login must also have the permissions needed to discover the objects in question.
Review source

column2: For a SQL database in the Fabric portal, access Copilot from the {{c1::query editor}}.
column3:
Open the SQL database in the Fabric portal and use Copilot from its query editor. You do not need to switch to an external SQL editor.
Review source

column2: Copilot in Fabric SQL database requires supported paid capacity rather than {{c1::trial capacity}}.
column3:
A trial does not qualify just because the workspace can run SQL queries. Copilot needs eligible paid capacity as well as the required tenant settings.
Review source
